## The High-Dimensional Trap
*Why volume concentrates in a thin shell and corners are empty.*

## Concentration of Measure
*Why random vectors are nearly orthogonal and Euclidean distances concentrate, with hubness as a consequence, which forces the approximate search of Chapter 4. Anisotropy, by contrast, is a property of trained spaces (Chapter 3).*

## Room for Exponentially Many Directions
*Why a space that holds only $D$ orthogonal vectors still holds exponentially many nearly orthogonal ones, the resource that distributed representations, superposition (Chapter 5), and hyperdimensional computing (Chapter 10) exploit, and dimensional collapse, in which a trained space uses only a few of those directions (Chapter 3).*

## The Johnson-Lindenstrauss Lemma
*The mathematical foundation preserving pairwise distances under random projections.*

## Random Walks in Many Dimensions
*Pólya's theorem (1921): a random walk returns home with certainty in one or two dimensions and only with probability less than one in three or more, so in high dimensions a walker is almost surely lost. After $n$ steps it is about $\sqrt{n}$ from the start and nearly orthogonal to where it began, concentration of measure seen as a process. On data the picture reverses: a walk confined to a neighbourhood graph cannot get lost, and its diffusion reveals the shape of the data (diffusion maps, Laplacian eigenmaps), which leads to the manifold hypothesis. The same walk reappears as a slowly drifting context vector that explains why word embeddings recover co-occurrence statistics (Chapter 3), and as the walks over a graph that DeepWalk and node2vec turn into sentences (Chapter 7).*

## The Manifold Hypothesis
*Why real-world data saves us from empty high-dimensional voids ($d_{\text{int}} \ll D_{\text{ambient}}$), a hypothesis that Chapter 8 tests with persistent homology.*

## An Aside on Optimization
*Why saddle points rather than poor local minima dominate high-dimensional loss landscapes, and what overparameterization changes. This concerns parameter space, not embedding space.*
